default.reason: Middle of the 3–4 bytes/token range typical for code; used for any language not listed

c.reason: Same as C++: similar syntax, identifier lengths and indentation in Ceph

cpp.reason: C++ sources and headers; equal to Go so that E is a plain byte ratio for C++ features; its error cancels for C++ features once E is recomputed with it, see the header comment

python.reason: Fewer braces and more words than C-family code, so slightly more bytes per token

shell.reason: Dense in symbols ($, quotes, pipes, flags), so slightly fewer bytes per token than C++

go.reason: Typical for Go; equal to C++, see the header comment. Used for rgw-go's sizes in calibration.yaml

rust.reason: More sigils and short keywords (&, ::, ', ?) than C++

java.reason: Long identifiers and verbose type names that tokenize into long pieces

javascript.reason: Similar to TypeScript with fewer long type annotations

html.reason: Markup is tag- and attribute-heavy, so it splits into many short tokens

css.reason: CSS and SCSS: selectors, numbers and units split into many short tokens

yaml.reason: Short keys, indentation and punctuation; sparser than code

json.reason: Quotes, colons and braces around short values; the most symbol-heavy format listed

cmake.reason: Function-call syntax with variable references; close to shell

markdown.reason: Mostly English prose, which tokenizes more densely than code

lua.reason: Similar to Python and C-family code

jinja.reason: Templates mix markup with {{ }} and {% %} delimiters

jsonnet.reason: Close to JSON, with fewer quotes

cython.reason: Python syntax with C type declarations; taken as Python

xml.reason: Tags and attributes split into many short tokens, as HTML does, with long repeated element names

ini.reason: Short key = value lines, close to YAML

toml.reason: Short key = value lines, close to YAML

cram.reason: Shell commands with their expected output; taken as shell

text.reason: Plain text files, mostly prose or word lists

expansion.reason: Product Go tokens rgw-go wrote per token of the v19.2.7 source it ported: its product Go over the size of that source times coverage, the share of it rgw-go has ported (calibration.yaml sizes and coverage). The sizes are measured; coverage is an assumption with a stated range. Every estimate scaled from rgw-go to Ceph is inversely proportional to the coverage it is computed at; rgw-go's own measured cost is not, and in the reference scenario the written translation is but the single read of the source is not. The product Go counts its comment lines, a large share of its bytes (calibration.yaml sizes.rgw_go.product_go_comments), many of them citing the C++ they replace, so this is tokens written per source token ported, not a code-size ratio.

test_ratio.reason: Test and tooling Go rgw-go wrote per token of its product Go (calibration.yaml sizes.rgw_go)

overhead.reason: Output tokens rgw-go's port emitted per token of Go that survived, product, test and tooling (calibration.yaml measurement.port and sizes.rgw_go). It pays for review passes, rework and discarded drafts, and for the Markdown the port produced and kept (plans and registers, calibration.yaml sizes.rgw_go.markdown), which is not counted as surviving Go

uncached_per_output.reason: Uncached input tokens per output token in rgw-go's port (calibration.yaml measurement.port)

cache_write_per_output.reason: Cache-write tokens per output token in rgw-go's port (calibration.yaml measurement.port)

cache_read_per_output.reason: Cache-read tokens per output token in rgw-go's port (calibration.yaml measurement.port); an agent re-reads its context on every call

source_read_passes.reason: Extra uncached reads of the source per unit of work. Zero here because the three measured ratios above already hold all of rgw-go's input; the naive scenario sets it to 1

config.reason: Configuration such as suite YAML is carried over almost mechanically. Its weight relative to the other classes is calibration.yaml ported_mix.relative_difficulty; this value is that weight divided by the relative scale's mean over the source rgw-go ported, so that the model applied to that source reproduces rgw-go's measured cost

glue.reason: Wiring, CLI plumbing and thin wrappers, which need much less reasoning than standard code. Its weight relative to the other classes is calibration.yaml ported_mix.relative_difficulty; this value is that weight divided by the relative scale's mean over the source rgw-go ported, so that the model applied to that source reproduces rgw-go's measured cost

standard.reason: The anchor of the scale is the average of what rgw-go ported: S3 request handling together with the byte-compatible RADOS layout, bucket index and class clients. This value is standard code's relative weight (calibration.yaml ported_mix.relative_difficulty) divided by the relative scale's mean over that source, so that the model applied to it reproduces rgw-go's measured cost

hard.reason: Consensus, PG peering and recovery, erasure coding, MDS cache and locking, the messenger and wire encodings: concurrency-heavy or protocol-critical code that needs more review and rework per line. Its weight relative to the other classes is calibration.yaml ported_mix.relative_difficulty; this value is that weight divided by the relative scale's mean over the source rgw-go ported, so that the model applied to that source reproduces rgw-go's measured cost

extreme.reason: BlueStore and BlueFS allocators and on-disk formats, Crimson and SeaStore: code where a subtle bug loses data, or whose design rests on a runtime the target lacks. Its weight relative to the other classes is calibration.yaml ported_mix.relative_difficulty; this value is that weight divided by the relative scale's mean over the source rgw-go ported, so that the model applied to that source reproduces rgw-go's measured cost

rust_factor.reason: Guess: Rust needs more tokens than Go for the same logic (lifetimes, explicit error types, async plumbing). Nothing measures it; rgw-rs is too small a spike

wasm_overhead.reason: Guess, applied uniformly to every feature on top of Rust. An adversarial review of this estimate (2026-11-14) reports that WASI lacks parallel threads, block devices and process execution, which would make shims and redesigns cost more; it rated those details plausible rather than confirmed, and no build for WASI was attempted to verify them. Host-side code that would stand in for what WASI cannot host is not costed

clean_break_discount.reason: Guess. Review of all kinds was 13% of rgw-go's cost (calibration.yaml derived.sanity_opus_5_5_usd.review_share); the share spent on byte-exact formats and coexistence was not measured.

long_cache_write_share.reason: Share of rgw-go's cache-write tokens written at the 1-hour lifetime (calibration.yaml measurement_detail.cache_write_ttl_tokens); applied unchanged to other models' long lifetime (e.g. Astra's 12h)

uncached.reason: Share of uncached input in calls whose prompt exceeds a model's long-context threshold. An agent run against a price sheet that surcharges long prompts would be configured to stay under the threshold. The share measured on rgw-go (calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.share_over_threshold), on a harness with a one-million-token window and no surcharge, is what a scenario applies when it takes prompts to be as long as rgw-go's; calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.long_context_scenarios names those scenarios. Either way the token volumes are held fixed, which a different prompt size would not do

cache_write.reason: Share of cache-write tokens in calls whose prompt exceeds a model's long-context threshold. An agent run against a price sheet that surcharges long prompts would be configured to stay under the threshold. The share measured on rgw-go (calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.share_over_threshold), on a harness with a one-million-token window and no surcharge, is what a scenario applies when it takes prompts to be as long as rgw-go's; calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.long_context_scenarios names those scenarios. Either way the token volumes are held fixed, which a different prompt size would not do

cache_read.reason: Share of cache-read tokens in calls whose prompt exceeds a model's long-context threshold. An agent run against a price sheet that surcharges long prompts would be configured to stay under the threshold. The share measured on rgw-go (calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.share_over_threshold), on a harness with a one-million-token window and no surcharge, is what a scenario applies when it takes prompts to be as long as rgw-go's; calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.long_context_scenarios names those scenarios. Either way the token volumes are held fixed, which a different prompt size would not do

output.reason: Share of output tokens in calls whose prompt exceeds a model's long-context threshold. An agent run against a price sheet that surcharges long prompts would be configured to stay under the threshold. The share measured on rgw-go (calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.share_over_threshold), on a harness with a one-million-token window and no surcharge, is what a scenario applies when it takes prompts to be as long as rgw-go's; calibration.yaml measurement_detail.prompt_size_tokens.long_context_scenarios names those scenarios. Either way the token volumes are held fixed, which a different prompt size would not do

fable-5-2.reason: No measurement of Fable 5.2's token use on this work; the same volumes are priced on its sheet. A model that needs more or less rework to reach the same result would cost more or less than shown

opus-5-5.reason: The calibration model, which ran nearly all of rgw-go's calls (calibration.yaml measurement.model_calls_share), so 1 by definition

gpt-6-astra.reason: No measurement of GPT-6 Astra's token use on this work; the same volumes are priced on its sheet. A model that needs more or less rework to reach the same result would cost more or less than shown

kimi-k3.reason: No measurement of Kimi K3's token use on this work; the same volumes are priced on its sheet. A model that needs more or less rework to reach the same result would cost more or less than shown

sloc_equivalent_bytes_per_line.reason: Bytes per code line of Ceph's own C++ in headline features of kind product, from data/generated/sloc.json through the taxonomy; cephest check recomputes it. A dependency's sloc_equivalent is in code lines, so each one carries the comments and blank lines real source does.

uncached.reason: Adjacent work (defect reproduction, security hook, PR servicing, feasibility) per unit of port work, in uncached input: the adjacent rows over the port row (calibration.yaml measurement). Only defect reproduction reported uncached input; the other three rows give none ("—" in the supplied table, counted as 0), so this is not a measurement of all four

cache_write.reason: Adjacent work (defect reproduction, security hook, PR servicing, feasibility) per unit of port work, in cache writes: the adjacent rows over the port row (calibration.yaml measurement)

cache_read.reason: Adjacent work (defect reproduction, security hook, PR servicing, feasibility) per unit of port work, in cache reads: the adjacent rows over the port row (calibration.yaml measurement)

output.reason: Adjacent work (defect reproduction, security hook, PR servicing, feasibility) per unit of port work, in output: the adjacent rows over the port row (calibration.yaml measurement)

optimistic.label: Optimistic
optimistic.description: Every feature costs what rgw-go's first implementation phase did per line, hard code is nearer to ordinary code than assumed, and rgw-go is taken at the top of its coverage range. The phase ratios are measured on rgw-go; that a whole port would sustain them, the difficulty and the coverage are assumptions.

calibrated.label: Scaled from rgw-go
calibrated.description: The token ratios one real port showed (rgw-go, to Go, on Claude Opus 5.5, unfinished), applied to every Ceph feature. Measured on rgw-go: output tokens per token of surviving Go, its test ratio and the ratio of each kind of input to output; assumed: that input grows in proportion to output, the share of radosgw rgw-go covers, the difficulty of each feature, the Rust and WASM factors, and that other models need the tokens Opus 5.5 did.

pessimistic.label: Pessimistic
pessimistic.description: Every feature costs what rgw-go's latest, review-heavier phase does per line, hard code is harder than assumed, rgw-go is taken at the low end of its coverage range, WASM needs a fifth more again, long prompts are billed at rgw-go's share where a price sheet surcharges them, and the work around the port (defect reproduction, security review, upstream PRs) is included. The phase ratios, the long-prompt shares and the adjacent work are measured on rgw-go; the difficulty, the coverage and the WASM factor are assumptions.

naive.label: Naive single pass
naive.description: A reference point, not an outcome: what a "translate every line once" estimate would say, with one pass over the source, no new tests, no review and no re-reading. It is shown for scale against the other scenarios; nothing about porting Ceph this way has been measured.
